projects.name: ReportLab
projects.governance_notes: Long-running commercial steward and named PyPI maintainers; production/stable package with an official security-focused 5.0 release line.
projects.why_relevant: The current deterministic one-page PDF renderer already uses it for text, shapes, and print-safe layout.
projects.age_fit: Neutral rendering infrastructure; Curiosity Engine owns elementary pedagogy, readability, and trust validation.
safety_notes: Use released packages, never repository tip.
Do not allow generated content to fetch arbitrary remote images or files.
The 5.0 release tightened remote-resource security defaults after a security review.

projects.name: Typst
projects.governance_notes: Company-led open-source project with sustained community contribution, public releases, and disclosed institutional funding for open work.
projects.why_relevant: Strong typesetting, reusable templates, math layout, and deterministic PDF-generation patterns.
projects.age_fit: Rendering infrastructure only; templates and generated pages still require first-grade readability and parent review.
safety_notes: Study stable release APIs and template patterns; do not install or execute automatically.
Review every third-party Typst package and asset under its own license.

projects.name: WeasyPrint
projects.governance_notes: Community project with professional maintenance/support by CourtBouillon, public changelogs, tests, and a long release history.
projects.why_relevant: Useful reference for paged HTML/CSS layout, accessibility-minded documents, and printable web styling.
projects.age_fit: Neutral document infrastructure; generated HTML and remote resources are untrusted input.
safety_notes: Reference only in the MVP because it adds native/system dependencies and URL-fetching risk.
Any future integration must disable arbitrary network fetches and pass SSRF-specific tests.

projects.name: OCRmyPDF
projects.governance_notes: Mature specialist project with documented maintainers, frequent releases, signed tags observed, contributor guidance, and professional support options.
projects.why_relevant: Mature local pipeline for adding searchable OCR text to scanned PDFs while retaining the original page image.
projects.age_fit: Good preprocessing reference for parent-provided worksheets; OCR output is evidence to verify, not ground truth.
safety_notes: Reference only until a sandboxed local adapter and malformed-PDF corpus exist.
Its system dependencies and subprocesses require pinned versions and resource limits.

projects.name: PaddleOCR
projects.governance_notes: Large active project overseen by the PaddlePaddle community/PMC with frequent public releases; size and model supply chain require added scrutiny.
projects.why_relevant: Actively maintained OCR and document-layout pipelines covering images, PDFs, tables, and many languages.
projects.age_fit: Potentially useful for worksheet photos and layout extraction; handwriting and early-reader worksheets need dedicated evals.
safety_notes: Large dependency and model-download surface; do not install during ordinary onboarding.
Evaluate model provenance, download hosts, local resource use, telemetry, and malformed inputs before promotion.
Never expose a distributed inference service on the family network by default.

projects.name: Tesseract OCR
projects.governance_notes: Long-lived widely used OCR project with named maintainers and a vulnerability-reporting document, although the reviewed support table needs updating.
projects.why_relevant: Long-lived local OCR baseline with broad language support and no hosted-family-data requirement.
projects.age_fit: Printed-text baseline only; not sufficient by itself for worksheet semantics, handwriting, or visual reasoning.
safety_notes: The reviewed SECURITY.md support table appears stale relative to current releases; require manual confirmation before integration.
Use packaged stable releases and isolate image parsing with size and time limits.

projects.name: Numbas
projects.governance_notes: Developed by Newcastle University's School of Mathematics, Statistics and Physics with tests, contributor guidance, and a current security-reporting route.
projects.why_relevant: University-governed patterns for parameterized math questions, marking, tests, schemas, and browser delivery.
projects.age_fit: Mechanics are useful, but the default ecosystem is not specifically first-grade; pedagogy and problem difficulty must be rebuilt and evaluated.
safety_notes: Study question-generation and validation patterns; do not import community-authored questions without separate license and quality review.
Do not run its compiler or expression language on untrusted input in the MVP.

projects.name: SymPy
projects.governance_notes: Established scientific Python community with broad institutional use, many contributors, public releases, and explicit contribution-quality rules.
projects.why_relevant: Credible symbolic mathematics engine for generating and independently checking exact arithmetic relationships.
projects.age_fit: Could validate generated elementary math, but it supplies mathematics rather than child-centered pedagogy.
safety_notes: Never parse or evaluate parent/model-provided expression strings as trusted SymPy code.
Promote only behind a tiny allowlisted arithmetic AST and adversarial parser tests.

projects.name: H5P Memory Game
projects.governance_notes: Official content type in the active H5P organization with a long commit history, localization, contribution rules, and accessibility-oriented implementation.
projects.why_relevant: A concrete, accessible HTML5 learning-game content type with semantic configuration and localization patterns.
projects.age_fit: Simple matching can fit early elementary when reading load, card count, time pressure, and feedback are parent-tuned.
safety_notes: Reference interaction and accessibility patterns only; the full H5P runtime is not an MVP dependency.
Images, audio, and authored game content each require their own rights and child-safety review.

projects.name: PhET Interactive Simulations
projects.governance_notes: University research/education project with documented development, code-review, licensing, cross-platform QA, and rigorously tested published simulations.
projects.why_relevant: Research-university examples of tested, inquiry-driven math and science simulations, including early-elementary number experiences.
projects.age_fit: Use the official simulation's stated grade level and parent preview; the organization covers a much wider age range.
safety_notes: PhET explicitly says repository main branches are unstable; link to rigorously tested published simulations or fixed release SHAs.
Individual simulations are commonly GPL-3.0 and media, third-party assets, PhET branding, and interoperable editions have separate terms.
Do not copy a simulation or asset merely because its source repository is public.

projects.name: Blockly
projects.governance_notes: Canonical project now maintained by the verified Raspberry Pi Foundation organization with scheduled releases, triage expectations, tests, and public compatibility policy.
projects.why_relevant: Foundation-maintained visual programming and interaction patterns that avoid syntax burden.
projects.age_fit: Potentially useful for parent-guided early-elementary sequencing games; not a default first-grade interface without usability testing.
safety_notes: The canonical repository moved from Google to Raspberry Pi Foundation; old links must not be treated as current.
The maintainers say production users should select a release, not main or beta APIs.

projects.name: Phaser
projects.governance_notes: Commercially maintained open-source engine with more than a decade of development, public releases, documentation, and a large contributor/user base.
projects.why_relevant: Long-lived, actively maintained 2D web-game engine with a stable public API and strong examples ecosystem.
projects.age_fit: Engine only; every game still needs an elementary learning objective, no dark patterns, no ads, accessibility, and parent review.
safety_notes: Use a stable tagged release, never an RC or repository HEAD.
Do not load third-party plugins, remote code, analytics, ads, accounts, or multiplayer services in child-facing artifacts.

projects.name: GDevelop
projects.publisher: Florian Rival, GDevelop Ltd., and community
projects.governance_notes: Founder/company-led project with a very active signed-release stream and public extension review labels, but a large mixed official/community ecosystem.
projects.why_relevant: Actively released visual game-creation environment with open engine, examples, and extension patterns.
projects.age_fit: Useful to study authoring and simple interactions, but it is a large general game platform rather than an elementary pedagogy system.
safety_notes: Large desktop/web application and extension ecosystem; do not install or run during ordinary family onboarding.
Official, experimental, community, premium, and third-party assets/extensions must be distinguished and separately vetted.
Generated games must exclude accounts, ads, purchases, multiplayer, analytics, and external links.

projects.name: Scratch Editor
projects.governance_notes: Nonprofit educational steward with a major child-creator community and active engineering, currently consolidating formerly separate repositories into a monorepo.
projects.why_relevant: Credible child-centered creative-coding interaction patterns and a major educational community.
projects.age_fit: Scratch primarily targets older elementary children; a first grader generally needs substantial adult support.
safety_notes: The former scratch-vm repository was archived after migration into this monorepo, which is still an evolving integration surface.
AGPL obligations, Scratch trademarks, community/network features, and child accounts require legal and privacy review.
Watch for design research only; not approved as an MVP dependency or generated-game runtime.
